summary_for_principal:
Small pre-built tools can now be composed into one bigger unit and run automatically end-to-end, in order, sharing intermediate results. This was refused outright until now, alongside making outside-service calls (already done last time).

A person- or AI-driven step inside a composed unit still surfaces for review the normal way. Also found and fixed a gap in the underlying file-format description that would have wrongly rejected a correctly-built composed unit.

interpretation.read_as: Implement WP-04 Part 2 largely as designed (compose.* namespace, engine-driven dispatch, CODE/EXTERNAL/SKILL-only composed children), departing from one specific design-document suggestion (nested-scope addressing for composed children) where building it out found that suggestion did not fit the shape it was meant for.

filled_in.gap: The WP-04 design document suggested addressing a composed child at a NESTED scope (`{scope}/{node_id}.compose[{i}]`), mirroring how a PROCESS call's own child steps are addressed (§9.3). Building it found this wrong for composes specifically: a nested scope's entire purpose is an independent node graph with its own start/nodes/endings for _resolve_scope to descend into — composes has none of that, it is a flat, fixed-length sequence.
filled_in.assumed: Address composed children flat, in the SAME scope string as the outer STEP (`{node_id}.compose[{i}]`), detected by report() via a new regex checked before the ordinary node lookup. Avoids extending _resolve_scope's own recursive-descent machinery for a graph shape that does not exist here.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'adopt the cheap seam now; defer the expensive guess' — the flat address is the smaller, more honest fit for a fixed sequence; nothing about composes needs a graph-shaped scope, so building one would be machinery for its own sake.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — the addressing scheme is internal (never exposed as a schema field); a future pass could still move to nested scoping without any definition author's YAML changing.

filled_in.gap: The design document said composed children's outputs are threaded through 'shared values' without naming the operational mapping mechanism a composite's own declared `output:` uses to read them back out.
filled_in.assumed: Reuse mechanism.result (the same result.outputs/result.endings shape a PROCESS call already uses, §9.1) rather than inventing a new field — the composite's own output IS a call result in the same sense a PROCESS call's is, just over children instead of a nested run. This required a real schema fix: the TOOL branch's own additionalProperties allowlist had never included result.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'hold conventions once' — reusing an existing, already-spec'd shape rather than introducing a second one that would mean the same thing.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — additive; a future field for composite-specific result mapping could be added without removing this one.

decisions.headline: D45 — mechanism.kind: TOOL (composite) is now dispatched by the engine, closing the TOOL half of D34: composes[] children run in declared order over a private compose.* run-state namespace, addressed flat (same scope as the outer STEP) rather than nested, with a child's own record written only on success.
decisions.problem: D34 refused TOOL (composite) as spec-silent on how children exchange state and whether a non-deterministic child's own hand-off should surface transparently or stay opaque. The design document answered both, but its own nested-scope addressing suggestion for the first question did not survive contact with composes' actual shape (a flat sequence, not a graph) once building it.
options_rejected: Nested-scope addressing as the design document proposed, extending _resolve_scope to recurse into composes: rejected — composes has no graph for _resolve_scope to descend into; the extension would be dead machinery for a shape that does not exist.

Increment a composed child's own attempt number on each retry, the same way a top-level STEP does: rejected — self-found during implementation to cause an infinite loop on composite-level TRANSIENT retry (a re-entered _advance_compose would find the failed child's prior attempt already recorded and re-propagate the same stale failure forever, never re-dispatching the child). Fixed by recording a composed child's own attempt only on success, at a fixed attempt=1 key.

Allow PROCESS or nested TOOL composed children: rejected — PROCESS's own output writing is state.*-only, a namespace mismatch with compose.* needing deeper engine changes; nested TOOL is explicitly out of scope in the design document itself. Both refused at validation (V17) and runtime (EngineRefusal), matching D26/D34/D38's own refuse-rather-than-guess precedent.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — _advance_compose/_report_compose_child/_apply_compose_output are additive, reached only for mechanism.kind: TOOL; the rewritten V17 and the schema's result allowlisting are both widenings with no durable-record shape change.

lessons.maxim: A design document's own suggested implementation shape is a proposal, not a spec commitment — read it against the actual data shape (here, a flat fixed-length sequence vs. a graph) before building it, not after.
lessons.incident: The WP-04 design document suggested nested-scope addressing for composed children, mirroring PROCESS's own precedent; building it found composes has no graph for a nested scope's own machinery (_resolve_scope's recursive descent) to serve, so the suggestion was dropped in favour of flat, same-scope addressing without loss of any capability the design actually needed.
